summary: Describes a Uniform Resource Name namespace for the Web3D Consortium, for naming lasting resources such as specifications, VRML and X3D files, and XML document type definitions. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A permanent name works like a person's full name, which stays the same even if they move. This memo sets up such names for 3D-web documents and files.

questions: what is the web3d urn namespace
how do you name x3d files
how does web3d organize resource names
subtitle: A permanent name registry for 3D web documents and resources.

tldr.problem: The Web3D Consortium creates 3D specifications and files (VRML, X3D) that need permanent, location-independent names so they are not lost if a website moves.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers a formal URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace called 'web3d' with a hierarchical structure where different Web3D working groups assign unique identifiers under their domain.
tldr.outcome: Organizations and developers can now use stable names like urn:web3d:x3d:schemas:2002:compact to reference Web3D resources, whether they are standards documents, 3D files or XML schemas, without fear of losing them to link rot.

today: RFC 3541 is an Internet Standard informational document and remains the formal registry for the web3d URN namespace. The Web3D Consortium continues to maintain the namespace and publish URN catalogs.

sections.title: What Web3D is and why it needs names
sections.content:
The Web3D Consortium is a non-profit that develops standards for 3D graphics on the web and in broadcast, including VRML97 (a 1997 standard for Virtual Reality) and its successor X3D. The Consortium also creates XML schemas, style sheets and media assets.

Web3D realized that many of its resources needed permanent names that would not break if a website moved. Developers were already using URN-style names in VRML files, but without a formal registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Web3D makes standards and files for showing 3D things online. They needed a way to give those files permanent names that would never break.

sections.title: URNs and the web3d namespace
sections.content:
A URN (Uniform Resource Name) is like a person's name: it identifies something, but does not say where to find it (unlike a URL, which is an address). The RFC registers the web3d URN namespace, which means any URN starting with urn:web3d: belongs to Web3D.

URNs under web3d follow a structure: urn:web3d:{subgroup}:{subgroup-specific string}. For example, urn:web3d:vrml97:node:GeoCoordinate names a GeoCoordinate node from the VRML97 standard, and urn:web3d:x3d:schemas:2002:compact names an X3D schema.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN is a permanent name. The web3d namespace is like a last name that groups all Web3D things together. Under that, different teams name their files in a way that makes sense to them.

sections.title: How the namespace is organized and managed
sections.content:
Web3D subgroups—such as the VRML97 group, the X3D group, and the Humanoid Animation Working Group—each manage the names under their part of the namespace. The chair of each subgroup assigns unique identifiers within their scope and publishes how their group's URNs are structured.

The Web3D Board of Directors ensures identifiers stay unique and maintains the persistence of all resources that receive a web3d URN. The Consortium publishes URN catalogs that map each name to a URL so people can look up where a named resource actually is.
sections.plainLanguage: Each Web3D team is in charge of names for their own work. The whole group promises to keep those names working forever.

sections.title: What the namespace covers
sections.content:
The web3d namespace applies to any resource Web3D produces or manages: technical documents and specifications, VRML and X3D files, XML Document Type Definitions (DTDs) and schemas, XML namespaces, style sheets, media assets and anything else the Consortium needs to name persistently.

The RFC is formal and global, not just for one website or project. Web3D resources named under this namespace are made freely available to the public.
sections.plainLanguage: This namespace can name anything Web3D makes: standards papers, 3D files, XML definitions, pictures, and more.
